What research and visual or aural sourcing means here: Timbre is sound quality—the set of audible features that helps two sources or actions sound different even at a similar pitch and loudness. How the relationship changes the result: The material and action shape a sound’s beginning, continuation, and ending. A quick tap has a sharp attack and short decay; rubbed paper has a softer attack and continuing noise. Choice and tradeoff: A dense mix can feel full but mask individual layers. A sparse texture reveals timbre clearly but may reduce weight or momentum. Worked example: Tap a tabletop once, then rub one sheet of paper for the same count. Map each as ATTACK → SUSTAIN → DECAY and cite the moment that distinguishes them. A trusted adult may produce the two sounds if needed. Non-example: Calling one source “better” or naming an instrument family without citing an audible or supplied source feature is preference or recall, not listening evidence. 1. A private self-critique receives full credit. 5. ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g11-arts-and-music-u01-l02

Lesson focus: research and visual or aural sourcing

Resource type: ACADEMY_ORIGINAL_MODEL

MODEL A — “One relationship at a time.” Timbre is sound quality—the set of audible features that helps two sources or actions sound different even at a similar pitch and loudness. The material and action shape a sound’s beginning, continuation, and ending. A quick tap has a sharp attack and short decay; rubbed paper has a softer attack and continuing noise. Worked example for research and visual or aural sourcing: Tap a tabletop once, then rub one sheet of paper for the same count. Map each as ATTACK → SUSTAIN → DECAY and cite the moment that distinguishes them. A trusted adult may produce the two sounds if needed. Starting state: state the intended effect, question, or criterion before acting. First decision: locate attack, sustain, decay, brightness, density, register, layer, and source action. Intermediate state: complete one bounded study, loop, map, or comparison while most features stay stable. Check: cite what changed before judging it. Finished or intentionally partial result: keep the evidence even when it challenges the first intention. Common misapplication: Calling one source “better” or naming an instrument family without citing an audible or supplied source feature is preference or recall, not listening evidence. Legitimate variation: another learner may choose different safe household sound or supplied event-map route, comparison order, quality words supported by evidence, layer to foreground, final listening or production revision and still meet the criterion. Use it to study research and visual or aural sourcing; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Academy-original Model A as the first model work; no outside search or teacher-supplied example is required.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: The submission contains the required work blocks and one reviewable process state; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.
The learner locates relevant attack, sustain, decay, brightness, density, register, layer, and source action and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.
The learner states an intent or claim and supports it with observable evidence while retaining ownership of artistic decisions.
The process record shows a check and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the result.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a labelled visual, tactile, constructed, or accessible digital work to preserve the making target; prose alone does not claim visual or material technique evidence. You may describe the work in writing and have one trusted adult verify a physical artifact without photographing you or your home. No microphone, camera, or recording is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task centres an aural element (research and visual or aural sourcing). Provide a fully equivalent non-aural route: notated, written, or graphic representation; visual or tactile pulse (a moving marker, a tapped or felt beat); and vibration or sight-reading in place of listening. Do not require the learner to hear a pitch, interval, or timbre to demonstrate understanding of it.

Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.fallback: Use the complete supplied beat map, script, evidence record, or event description. No teacher handout or outside search is required.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce research and visual or aural sourcing to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one attack relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact attack evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from attack, sustain, decay, brightness, density, register, layer, and source action; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply research and visual or aural sourcing under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on research and visual or aural sourcing rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
